problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $P(x).$

feedback.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-3,{x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $5.$ Find $P(x).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-3$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=5,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =5(x-(-3))(x-(-3))(x-1) \\  & =5(x+3)(x+3)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}5(x+3)(x+3)(x-1) & =5({x}^{2}+6x+9)(x-1) \\  & =5({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}+6{x}^{2}-6x+9x-9) \\  & =5({x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}+3x-9) \\  & =5{x}^{3}+25{x}^{2}+15x-45.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=5{x}^{3}+25{x}^{2}+15x-45.$
